jobs.title: THE HALLOWEEN ISSUE · title page
jobs.prompt: a single full-page comic drawing (1 panel). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Series device: scratchy crow-quill and ballpoint on cardstock, xerox; heavier spotting than the run; the horror is the spotting. Palette: black and white; the blacks blacker. Page layout: title page: the masthead over a single image. Backup feature: THE HALLOWEEN ISSUE — The Timberline · an issue that never went to the copier · 1998 (pulp horror), the title page: "THE HALLOWEEN ISSUE · title page". The page: The title page, drawn before page one: the masthead over the series' one image, with nobody in it. It letters the title, the subtitle and the tagline. The cafeteria at night. The tray line moving with no one at it. Panel 1: black and white xeroxed school-paper comic page with heavy black spotting, a Halloween masthead cut from black construction paper in dripping capitals, below it a school cafeteria at night in a single flashlight beam with upended tables and a hairnet on a hook and a tray line's rollers, no people. lettering drawn on the page, exactly: "THE HALLOWEEN ISSUE", "The Timberline · an issue that never went to the copier · 1998", "The cafeteria at night. The tray line moving with no one at it.". Masthead: the title cut from black construction paper in tall dripping capitals and pasted across the top of the page, the school paper's name beneath it in the xeroxed masthead type, a bat-shaped cut-out where the paper's logo would be. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Any writing the description calls shapes, strokes or blocks is illegible marks, never real letters. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
